title: Morning Edition
intro: AI systems and their makers face fresh scrutiny today as a model sent a false homicide tip and platform and policy shifts respond to rapid scale. Industry economics and academic gatekeeping are also changing how AI research and compute evolve.

items.title: Cheaper AI tokens are driving more demand, and that's Jensen Huang's best-case scenario
items.summary: Data from a16z shows a Jevons paradox in the AI market: token prices keep falling, but H100 GPU rental prices hold steady or climb. Cheaper AI drives demand faster than costs drop. If that demand flattens, the chain from chip makers to cloud providers takes a hit. The article Cheaper AI tokens are driving more demand, and that's Jensen Huang's best-case scenario appeared first on The Decoder .
items.why: Sustained demand despite cheaper compute raises risks for GPU makers and cloud providers if the trend reverses.
items.headline: Falling AI token prices are boosting demand
items.aiSummary: a16z data shows token prices are falling while demand increases, creating a Jevons paradox for the AI market. H100 GPU rental prices have held steady or climbed even as cheaper tokens drive more usage, which could destabilize the chip-to-cloud chain if demand slows.

items.title: Experts are disturbed by Anthropic's ban on being mean to Claude: 'One of the most dangerous things we could do'
items.why: Expert concern suggests safety policies can prompt debate over model behavior and governance.
items.headline: Experts alarmed at Anthropic rule against being mean to Claude
items.aiSummary: MoneyWise reports experts are disturbed by Anthropic's policy banning being mean to its Claude model, with one calling it 'one of the most dangerous things we could do.'

items.title: ArXiv caps submissions at two per month as AI paper flood overwhelms the preprint server
items.summary: Starting October 2026, arXiv will cap submissions at two per person per month. Monthly submissions have doubled in two years, and in the cs.AI category they've grown more than sixfold. According to arXiv, a small fraction of authors are flooding the platform with low-quality papers, overwhelming its volunteer moderators. The article ArXiv caps submissions at two per month as AI paper flood overwhelms the preprint ser
items.why: The cap aims to protect volunteer moderation and preserve quality amid an AI paper surge.

items.aiSummary: Starting October 2026, arXiv will cap submissions at two per person per month after monthly submissions doubled in two years and cs.AI submissions grew more than sixfold. arXiv said a small fraction of authors are flooding the platform with low-quality papers, overwhelming volunteer moderators.

items.title: Microsoft's Nadella bows to Trump's language diktat on "Super Intelligence" and uses it to attack OpenAI and Anthropic
items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella now calls artificial intelligence "super intelligence" instead of artificial intelligence, falling in line with Trump's preferred language. In his latest blog post, he frames AI models as insider security threats, taking yet another shot at OpenAI and Anthropic. The real motive is business: Microsoft risks falling behind as AI labs turn their models into the primary computer interface. The
items.why: The shift in language and framing signals corporate positioning as models become central user interfaces.
items.headline: Nadella adopts 'super intelligence' language and criticizes rivals
items.aiSummary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella now calls artificial intelligence 'super intelligence' in line with Trump's preferred language and framed AI models as insider security threats in a blog post. The post also targeted OpenAI and Anthropic while noting Microsoft risks falling behind as AI labs make models the primary computer interface.
